data.headline: Fed minutes show a split over how soon to raise rates
data.summary: The minutes released Wednesday describe the October 27–28 meeting. Most participants supported holding the federal funds target at 3.75% to 4.00%. Some favored a quarter-point increase. That disagreement matters to long bonds because expected future short rates help shape long yields.

bull.text: Participants who favored waiting cited the need to see how the September rate increase would pass through the economy.

bear.text: Some participants favored another 25-basis-point increase in October, citing persistent inflation and the risk that a later response would need to be larger.

watch.text: Leveraged funds were net short 149,858 Treasury bond futures contracts on November 10, down from 166,257 a week earlier. Both observations preceded publication of the minutes.

limitations: The minutes record views at the October meeting. Future policy decisions depend on later information. The CFTC series covers Treasury bond futures. TLT’s daily outcome requires the fund’s regular-session opening and closing prices.
